description: A thicket-forming shrub 2-4 m tall whose young stems are bright red, with oval leaves in pairs whose veins curve toward the tip, flat clusters of small white flowers in late spring and bunches of white berries in late summer. It lines the banks of the permanent creeks and pond shores, and its red stems are the brightest colour along the water in winter.

season_notes.winter: Bare stems glowing red to purple-red along the creek, the most colourful thing in the winter riparian.
season_notes.spring: Leaves out in March and April; flat white flower clusters in May and June.
season_notes.summer: Dense green thicket; the berries ripen white to bluish-white from July and are stripped quickly by birds.
season_notes.fall: Leaves turn red to purple-red before they drop in November.

riparian.water: Wants permanently moist to wet soil with its roots near the water: the banks of creeks that run all year, springs and pond shores.

notes: Creek (red osier, American) dogwood, Cornus sericea (C. stolonifera in older floras; the Sierra plants include ssp. sericea and the hairier ssp. occidentalis), is a deciduous thicket shrub 1.5-5 m of permanently moist streambanks, springs, wet meadows and pond shores from the foothills to the subalpine. It spreads by stolons and by stems that arch over and root where they touch, so a plant becomes a thicket. Form: plain 'shrub'. Eight to fourteen slender stems (radius_ratio 0.012) lean out and arch (trunk curve 22, stem_spread 44, level-1 droop), opposite branching (rotation -90 on both levels), a rounded thicket wider than tall, leafy to the ground (envelope base 0.42). Young stems smooth, bright red to purple-red, old ones grey-brown: bark_rgb and twig_rgb the red of the young stems, and winter_twigs 0.65 with a red winter tint because the bare red thicket is the plant's winter look; the old class has grey-brown dead stems inside. Leaves opposite, oval to lanceolate, 5-10 cm, with five to seven veins curving toward the tip, dark green above, pale beneath: leaf_shape oval, leaf_size_m 0.08, a fifth of the palette lightened. Flowers small, white, in flat-topped clusters 3-6 cm, May-June (some again later): flowers cluster. Fruit a white to bluish-white berry-like drupe 7-9 mm in clusters, July-October, eaten quickly by birds and mammals. Fall colour red to purple (r/g about 2.6). Zones: bank and pond shore, the margin second, terrace little; perennial water; orders [2, 6]. Architectural model provisional.
